make casks.text: Casks and barrels are assembled by coopers using sturdy wooden staves, bound tightly together with iron or wooden hoops. The natural swelling of the damp wood ensures a watertight seal, making these vessels essential for the storage and long-distance transport of liquids such as beer, wine, and salted provisions.

knit garments.text: Knitting utilizes long wooden or bone needles to interlock loops of spun yarn into a flexible, continuous fabric. This method produces warm, form-fitting garments that provide excellent insulation against harsh winter drafts, serving as essential clothing for commoners and gentry alike.

fishing.text: Fishermen cast nets and set lines from small boats or coastal shacks to draw a harvest from the sea. This arduous toil provides a vital source of fresh protein for the parish, though the catch must be consumed quickly or cured before spoilage sets in.

inputs.timber: Timber is used to keep the fishing boats in good repair.
inputs.tar: The boat's tar coating wears off over time and needs to be replaced.

maintain.text: Significant work is needed to keep the park looking good and adding to the beauty of the town.

hold feast.text: Hosting a feast requires the provision of plentiful food and drink for guests drawn from the local community. Such gatherings are a tangible demonstration of surplus and generosity, elevating the household's standing and securing the goodwill of the parish.

hold banquet.text: The grand banquet is an opulent display of excess, reserved for the upper echelons of the nobility and high gentry. By presenting exotic dishes, premium vintages, and elaborate entertainment, the host projects undeniable wealth and generosity, resulting in an elevation of their social standing.

craft cookware.text: Essential for both the humble hearth and the industrial kitchen, cookware is crafted by working copper into robust vessels. These pots and cauldrons are designed to withstand repeated exposure to open flame, efficiently transferring heat for boiling, stewing, and rendering.

inputs.tin ingots: A tin coating protects the copper from reacting with the content, extending the lifetime of the vessels and avoiding contamination. Tin can also be used to solder copper elements together and seal joints.
inputs.silver bars: A silver lining improves both the function and aesthetics of the cookware. Silver can also be used to solder copper elements together and seal joints.
inputs.lead bars: Lead is melted and mixed with tin or silver to lower the melting point and make it easier to work with, both for soldering and coating.

salt meat.text: Cuts of fresh meat are packed into sturdy timber casks with generous layers of coarse salt. The salt rapidly draws out moisture, halting the putrefaction of the flesh and transforming the perishable meat into a durable provision suited for long winters or arduous maritime journeys.

brew hop beer.text: The addition of hops to the boiling malt wort introduces a sharp, bitter balance to the sweet liquid.

build hulk.text: The hulk is a massive, broad-beamed vessel built with overlapping timber planks in the clinker fashion. Its high, rounded sides maximize cargo space, while its sturdy masts carry the large square sails necessary to drive this heavy workhorse of maritime trade across open waters.

sew sails.text: Within the wide floors of the sail loft, heavy canvas is cut and stitched into massive sails. The workers use thick thread and specialized leather palms to drive needles through the dense weave, heavily reinforcing the seams to withstand the tearing force of coastal gales.

trap fish.text: Woven from pliable willow or reeds, fish traps are staked in tidal shallows and river currents. The funneled entrances guide the fish into a holding chamber from which they cannot navigate an escape, providing a steady and reliable yield of fresh fish with little ongoing exertion.

let rowhouses.text: Rowhouses are let out, providing dense and efficient housing for the growing population of urban commoners and craftsmen. By sharing common walls, these timber-framed dwellings conserve heat and building materials, offering an affordable residence close to the markets and workshops.

protect.text: Armed guards and constables are hired to protect the town's valuable assets and maintain order within the parish. Equipped with sturdy armour and sharp weapons, they patrol the streets and secure the storehouses against theft and disruption, ensuring that trade and production continue unimpeded.

prepare rigging.text: Rigging is prepared by systematically cutting and splicing heavy rope to form the intricate network of lines required for a ship. The standing rigging is secured to support the masts, while tackles and blocks are assembled into the running rigging, providing the sailors with the mechanical advantage needed to hoist and trim the massive sails.

make maille.text: Thousands of small iron or steel rings are meticulously linked and riveted together to form a flexible mesh of maille armour. This dense, heavy fabric of metal offers excellent protection against slashing blows while maintaining enough flexibility for the wearer to move unhindered in combat.

shovel manure.text: Manure is collected from the stables and sheds where livestock are kept, then shovelled into carts or pits for aging. This nutrient-rich waste is a vital resource for the parish farms, as working it into the soil replenishes exhausted fields and significantly improves the yield of upcoming harvests.

shovel muck.text: Manure and muck are collected from the stables and sheds where livestock are kept, then shovelled into carts or pits for aging. This nutrient-rich waste is a vital resource for the parish farms, as working it into the soil replenishes exhausted fields and significantly improves the yield of upcoming harvests.

ripple flax.text: Rippling is the process of drawing dried flax stalks through a heavy comb-like tool, or ripple, to detach the seed bolls from the stems. This must be done prior to retting to prevent the seeds from rotting in the water. The collected seeds are saved for sowing or oil crushing, while the clean stalks are prepared for further fibre processing.

inputs.tools: Iron-toothed ripples allow for swifter and more thorough extraction of the seeds from the flax stalks, reducing the labour required.

collect slabs.text: Slabs are the rounded, bark-covered outer cuts of logs discarded during squaring at the sawmill. By collecting these waste pieces from the yard and sawing them down, labourers can produce a cheap supply of firewood without the need to fell additional trees.

inputs.tools: Iron saws and axes enable the labourers to cut and split the awkward, bark-covered slabs much faster and with greater ease.

inscribe books.text: Scribes copy and ornament manuscripts by hand. Each page is inscribed and bound between protective covers, producing enduring volumes of knowledge and devotion that elevate the standing of the monastery.

inputs.gold bars: Beaten gold leaf is applied by the illuminator to initial letters and borders to catch the light.
inputs.premium dye: Vibrant and rare pigments are used to illustrate elaborate miniatures and margins.
inputs.leather: Tanned leather hides are wrapped around wooden boards to create a durable, protective cover.
inputs.paper: Individual sheets of paper are folded and sewn together to form the body of the book.
inputs.thread: Strong linen thread is used to sew the folded sheets of paper into individual gatherings or signatures.

hammer alembics.text: Alembics are specialized distillation vessels crafted by coppersmiths from sheets of hammered copper. The coppersmith shapes the spherical cucurbit and the helm, using solder to join the components into a vapour-tight seal. These vessels are essential for the distillation of spirits, perfumes, and chemical acids.

inputs.copper ingots: Refined copper is hammered into thin, malleable sheets to form the body and neck of the alembic.
inputs.lead bars: Lead is melted and mixed with tin or silver to lower the melting point and make it easier to work with, both for soldering and coating.
inputs.tin ingots: Tin is alloyed with lead to formulate a low-melting-point solder that flows easily into the seams of the copper joints.
inputs.silver bars: Silver is used to line or ornament the alembics, preventing copper corrosion from reactive distillates, and can also be used as a solder to seal joints.

boil soap.text: Soap is produced by boiling tallow and potash lye in large cauldrons, initiating the saponification process that turns fat into cleanser. Once boiled, the thick soap is poured into moulds or casks to cool, solidify, and age. The resulting blocks are sliced into bars, offering a highly sought-after commodity for laundry, scouring wool, and personal cleanliness.

inputs.tallow: Rendered animal fat provides the greasy base that chemically reacts with the alkali to form solid soap.
inputs.potash: Wood-ash potash acts as the caustic alkaline agent necessary to saponify the fat into soap.
inputs.flax plants: Flax flowers are added for colouring and scent.
inputs.herbs: Aromatic herbs are infused during boiling to scent the soap, masking the odour of the tallow and appealing to gentry clients.
inputs.dye: Adding colouring agents produces decorative, marbled soaps that command a higher standing.
inputs.casks: The hot liquid soap is poured into casks to cool, cure, and harden into bulk blocks for transport.
